description: Bell-shaped relic stupa on a stepped square terrace, tapering through stacked rings to a slender gilded finial spire.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Bell-shaped relic stupa rising from a stepped square terrace, rounded bell drum above a set of receding square plinths, a stack of narrowing horizontal rings above the bell tapering to a long slender needle finial, small niched alcove on each face of the base Materials: Whitewashed lime plaster crazed and flaking to grey render beneath, gilded finial with tarnished dull patches, dark rain streaking down the bell, moss in the terrace joints.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT (third build). Overall visual fidelity 0.91 -- silhouette 0.94, bell and spire 0.92, terrace and niches 0.90, palette 0.88, weighted by tier. 8,312/16,000 triangles, 7/12 draw calls, 4/8 materials, 7/32 unique geometries, 2 canvas textures.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at exactly 7.00 x 14.00 x 7.00 m against the re-declared 7 x 14 x 7 (the footprint follows the Meshy proxy's halfX 3.42-3.50 at the kept 14 m; the old 8 m was a list-time estimate). Area-weighted band comparison against the proxy (scratch/_mon/bands.mjs) gives mean |delta width| 0.012 and |delta depth| 0.011 of height, from 0.019 / 0.018; bands 3-9 -- everything above the terrace -- are within 0.010, where the second build had band 3 at +0.044 and band 5 at +0.032.
featureReviews.notes: The residual is bands 0-1 at -0.04, the terrace, where the 5-95 percentile of a three-step redented plan reads whichever slab tops are widest; the first emit of this build had the storey at 2.72 and measured -0.07 there, and refitting the storey to 3.00 with a 0.37 redent (corner reach 3.63 against the proxy's r95 3.60) halved it. Not chased further: bands 0-2 on a terraced base are dominated by ledge area, not by edge position.

featureReviews.evidence: Bell as one 40-segment lathe through the proxy's own radius-by-height: torus band 2.58, waist 2.28, body 2.36 at 4.15 to 1.90 at 6.40, dome through 1.58 (7.15), 1.28 (7.40), 0.93 (7.62), 0.71 (7.87) on a Catmull-Rom, neck 0.55 to 8.25 inside a 1.46 m harmika CUBE seated from 7.45 (dome meets its corners at 7.57, its faces at 7.85) under a cornice stepping out to 1.84 and a 1.68 top slab to 8.93. Spire 0.62(+0.06) at 8.85 to 0.20 at 12.30, sixteen rings, bands 6-8 within +0.010; finial 0.19 collar through the proxy's 0.17 / 0.12 / 0.08 to a bud at 14.00.
featureReviews.notes: The second build's harmika was a 2.10 m block UNDER a 1.52 m cube on a flat 1.30 m crown -- a crate on a hemisphere. The plate's bell crop and the proxy (halfX 0.77 at 8.13 rising to 0.83 at 8.5) both have the cap WIDER than the cube and the cube sunk into a domed shoulder, which is what is built. The domed-cone shoulder the second build rejected was rejected with the oversize block on it; with the cube at the proxy's size the same proxy profile is the plate's bell. Below 0.95 because the plate's foot rings are a shade heavier than the proxy's 2.58 band and the harmika cornice's two fillets are read off the plate, not measured.

featureReviews.evidence: Eight redented slabs (half-widths 3.50 / 3.42 / 3.32 / 3.20 / 3.00 storey / 3.12 / 3.22 / 2.77, redents 0.22 to 0.37) plus a round 2.63 m stone plinth in one merge; four instanced ROUND-HEADED aedicules 1.50 wide from 0.80 to 2.72, standing 0.43 m proud of the storey (front at 3.43 against the proxy's face reach 3.42), each with an 0.84 m round-arched aperture from a 0.50 sill and a shadow panel 0.52 m behind the front plane. Depth-map check: the proxy's +Z map reads the aedicule 1.6-1.8 x 2.2 m; the plate's base crop 1.6 x 2.2.
featureReviews.notes: The second build's terrace was six two-step slabs stepping evenly in from 4.00, with a 1.45 m square frame holding a 0.90 m hole. The plate's base crop shows stout three-step corner piers, a tall storey, cornice courses stepping OUT and a free-standing arched hoop per face; the proxy's per-slice r95 falling 4.67 -> 3.60 while halfX holds at 3.4-3.5 is the same reading -- faces barely step in, corners cut back deeper with height. Residuals: the plate's hoop is thicker than the 0.33 m rim built here, and its plinth mouldings carry a small cyma the slabs do not.

featureReviews.evidence: Four materials, every albedo the inverse of a PROBED transfer: a flat-material bundle of the second build was rendered and probed (stucco lit flank 1.096x authored, stone lit face 1.00x, stone tops 1.18x, gold 0.92x), and the plate's own readings (whitewash 208, pier 191, ledge 172, gilt #8E7950) divided through. Rendered: bell lit 191 (plate 208 clean, ~195 region), terrace 169 / tops 164 (plate 191 / 172), gold #8F7742 (plate #8E7950). Two post-construction Canvas 2D tiles: stucco with a two-level jittered-grid crack NETWORK plus a denser zoned pass, jagged-polygon flakes with a rim at 0.80 / 0.70, clustered thin drips at 0.78; stone at the terrace's exact 3.30 m height so its moss speck bands land on the seven real joints, over blurred drift, crazing and grain. Ledge tops carry a 0.76 vertex tint.
featureReviews.notes: The second build read as beige plaster with polka-dot flakes: #A7A7A1 authored as a "weathered mid grey" rendered 153, its 640 short crack walks read as scratches, and its layered disc flakes as spots. Two false starts this round are recorded because they will recur: eighteen flakes per tile (x4.4 round the bell) read as camouflage and went to four; disc-union flakes read as clouds and became angular polygons, which is how render actually breaks along its crazing. Below 0.90 because the harness's hemisphere fill renders the shaded flank at 156 where the plate reads 116 (unauthorable without darkening the lit face), and the drips are fainter than the plate's.

name: Chedi
notes: Vertically the tallest thing in a village skyline, so the readable feature is the profile: stepped square base, rounded bell, ringed taper, needle spire. That silhouette must survive at distance where no surface detail is visible at all. Collider is a cylinder rather than the building-part default box because the bell and spire are round in plan and a box proxy would leave a player colliding with empty air at the corners. Declared at 14 m, above the building-part category 8 m prior, which is correct for a village chedi -- a monastery one is far larger still. No destruction groups: it is static landmark geometry. Width and depth re-declared 8 -> 7 m (2026-09-02, third build): the Meshy proxy scaled to the kept 14 m height has its terrace at half-width 3.50 m on every slice from 0 to 2.9 m (scratch/_mon/profile.mjs, 56 slices), i.e. w:h = 0.50; a plate solve on the bottom slab edges (side 411 px against a 900-920 px height at el 30-35) gives 6.2-6.6 m. The proxy bbox wins, as it did for the Khmer sanctuary; the old 8 m made the base a squat pyramid the plate does not show.
